exposure: Patient perspectives on cervical length screening
outcome: Barriers to cervical length screening for preterm birth prevention
cohort: The study included 40 pregnant women up to 24 weeks gestation for interviews (Phase I) and 400 participants for questionnaire administration (Phase III) at a tertiary hospital in Thailand.
finding: Major barriers to universal cervical length screening for preterm birth prevention were identified as insufficient physician explanation, a poorly established government policy on prevention, and the costs associated with screening and treatment.
